chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Ja'far ibn Ali said:

I saw Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) prostrating after the prayer, so he spread his forearms on the ground and pressed his forehead (glabella) to the ground while still in his clothes. This is specific to the prostration of gratitude, distinct from the prostration that is within the prayer, because the Sunnah in the latter is for the person to be flat on the ground. He explained what we mentioned, what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: How should one perform the prostration of gratitude after prayer according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the distinct physical etiquette of *Sajdat al-Shukr*, where the Imam (AS) prostrated with arms spread and forehead pressed firmly to the ground while remaining clothed. This practice underscores the Shia scholarly distinction between the obligatory, formal prostrations of Salah and the voluntary, expressive prostration of gratitude, emphasizing humility and physical submission outside the strict ritual constraints of the prayer unit.
